newsitem.title: FRANCE: Truckers set up barricades at French borders.
newsitem.headline: Truckers set up barricades at French borders.

text.p: Truckers set up dozens of barricades around France and at borders on Monday as part of a European day of action for higher pay and harmonised working conditions in the European Union.

Drivers parked lorries on roads leading to Spanish, Italian, German and Swiss borders, often working with colleagues across the frontiers. The blockades caused long tailbacks, and in many places only cars were allowed to pass.
Dozens of other blockades disrupted roads in France, forcing long delays as part of a European Union drive for clearer work rules. In central France, truckers blocked a fuel depot near Brive.
"We work 80 hours, we get paid 56 at the most," said Roger Poletti, secretary general of the truckers' section of the independent Force Ouvriere union.

"There's not just driving. there's waiting time -- loading, loading, customs operations, etc, etc. There are plenty of other jobs that the bosses don't pay for and don't want to take into account," he told Europe 1 radio.
In the south-west, truckers blocked the Biriatou crossing to Spain, forcing cars to be diverted around Saint-Jean-de-Luz on the Atlantic.

A truck across the road blocked the access to the Mont Blanc tunnel in the Alps, letting only small vehicles drive through to Italy. A dozen trucks completely blocked the road leading to the Frejus tunnel linking France and Italy.

Near Strasbourg in eastern France, French and German truckers set up a barrier on a bridge over the Rhine. French and Swiss truckers also blocked a crossing at the Saint-Louis-Basle, leading to a two km (1.5 mile) tailback.

French truckers accuse bosses of failing to respect a deal last year cutting the retirement age to 55 from 60 for drivers with 25 years experience, as well as providing for sick pay, travel expenses, union rights and a ban on Sunday driving.
